text.en:
Kabir looked at the clock on the wall. The short hand pointed at 7 and the long hand pointed at 12.
"It is 7 o'clock!" said Amma. "School bus comes at half past 7."
Kabir wondered how long he had. He wanted to read the clock like a grown-up.
Can you help him?

A clock has two hands.
The short hand is the hour hand. It tells the hour.
The long hand is the minute hand.
When the minute hand points at 12, it is o'clock. The hour hand tells which hour: hour hand on 7 means 7 o'clock.
When the minute hand points at 6, it is half past. Hour hand just after 7 means half past 7.
There are 60 minutes in 1 hour, and half an hour is 30 minutes.
There are 24 hours in a day and 7 days in a week.
Look at a clock. The short hand is the hour hand. The long hand is the minute hand.
When the long hand is on 12, we say o'clock. Short hand on 3 means 3 o'clock.
When the long hand is on 6, we say half past. Half an hour is 30 minutes.
One hour has 60 minutes. One day has 24 hours. One week has 7 days.

problem.en: The school bus comes at half past 7. It is 7 o'clock now. How many minutes must Kabir wait?

text.en: From 7 o'clock to half past 7, the minute hand goes from 12 to 6.

why.en: o'clock is the minute hand on 12; half past is on 6.
An hour has 60 minutes and half of 60 is 30.

text.en: So Kabir must wait 30 minutes for the bus.

prompt.en: Your younger brother mixes up the two hands of the clock. How will you explain them?

requiredIdeas.en: The short hand is the hour hand.
The long hand is the minute hand.
Long hand on 12 means o'clock; on 6 means half past.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the long hand tells the hour.

points.en: The short hand tells the hour and the long hand tells the minutes.
Minute hand on 12 is o'clock; on 6 is half past.
1 hour = 60 minutes, half an hour = 30 minutes, 1 day = 24 hours, 1 week = 7 days.
